text: Are the stereotypes about women true? I continue with my take on stereotypes she is talking about. Number four. Women are so emotional. This is the one I hear the most and it's honestly so funny. Are women the ones taking pew-pews to school or movie theaters or grocery stores? Have you ever seen a woman punch a hole through a wall just because her favorite sports team didn't win? Are women starting literal wars because they can't figure out how to negotiate with other world leaders? I don't think so. I believe with her argument she wants to say that men are actually more emotional than women. That's a rather strong claim. Are women emotional? Yes, they are. Are men emotional? Yes, they are. Now, who is more emotional is a rather difficult question as it depends a lot on what emotional even means. If by emotional we mean things like anxiety, mood swings, emotional sensitivity, and empathy, then psychology research is actually quite consistent on this. Across large studies using the big five personality model, women on average score higher in neuroticism, which is basically the tendency to experience negative emotions like stress, worry, and emotional reactivity. This has been replicated across cultures and countries for decades. Women also tend to be more emotionally expressive. They talk about their feelings more openly and report them more. But that's only half of the picture. Men are emotional too, just differently. Men are more likely to experience and express emotions like anger, frustration, and aggression. And instead of talking about emotions, they are more likely to act on them. So once again, who is more emotional, men or women, would depend a lot on the definition of the term emotional. Miss, I don't know which world do you live in, but in today's world, it is common for both partners to work, to manage the house, and to take care of kids. And how is that even related to gold digging? And since you didn't really address this stereotype, let me do the job for you. First, we need to define who is a gold digger. I suggest this definition. It is a person who pursues romantic relationship primarily for financial gain or material benefits rather than genuine emotional connection or attraction. Are there women whose primarily purpose when looking for a guy is material benefits? For sure there are. But it is hard to say how many women are like that as there is no credible research on gold diggers since this concept is too vague and subjective. If you ask me, based on my experience, most women are not gold diggers. Most of them do want genuine emotional connection and attraction. With that said, hypergamy is still a thing. In simple terms, it means that on average, women tend to date across or up, especially when it comes to income, status, and overall stability. But that has very little to do with gold digging. It is more about general preferences, the same way men, on average, tend to date across or down, often placing more emphasis on youth and attractiveness.
